assertion.statement: Nested unnormalized corestrictions of the actual class equal direct corestriction, and commute with its equivariant character coefficient push; no field-degree factor is introduced.
assertion.objects: The actual retained finite-coefficient Kato classes, their coefficient-character push and the nested finite conductor fields.
assertion.hypotheses: Open finite-index subgroups for the stated conductor fields; the same original class and equivariant coefficient push at every finite coefficient level. Inverse-limit passage is separately supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: All groups, modules and degrees in the stated source scope.
assertion.parameter_range: The indicated section of the published2006 Selmer Complexes.
assertion.uniformity: Functorial cohomological maps; no arithmetic bound is asserted.
assertion.normalizations: Exactly the induced-module, coset and coefficient conventions in the cited source.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No arithmetic inertia condition, actual Euler system or newform is supplied.
assertion.limit_order: Apply Section8.1.4 at finite discrete coefficient level. Any later compatible inverse-limit passage remains a separate supplied input.

use.reason: Use product coset representatives for the nested subgroups in the finite sum of8.1.4. The two finite sums are the direct sum term by term. An equivariant coefficient map commutes with every summand. Pass only through the already compatible finite coefficient systems; no cor-restriction identity or degree division is used.
use.shared_contract_justification: Both occurrences compare the same retained class by nested finite-field corestriction before the already justified inverse limit.

supplier.statement: The finite coset sum in Section8.1.4 defines a cochain map inducing corestriction, independent of the chosen coset section up to homotopy; nested sections make corestriction transitive.
